authority_classes.duplicate-authority: two homes own or compute the same state or value; one must become a read
authority_classes.aggregation: detailed and aggregate computations coexist legitimately: one owner holds the state and the aggregation interface is documented (refinement B)
authority_classes.mixed: part legitimate aggregation, part duplicate authority
authority_classes.ownership-gap: no owner, or the owner sits in the wrong engine
authority_classes.shared-part: distinct mechanisms that should share a helper or a boundary contract

edge_types.depends_on: from reads an output of to (resolved from the dependency field)
edge_types.restates: from is a doc/adapter restating the authoritative mechanism to
edge_types.overlap: from and to are in the same overlap group (to = first member)
edge_types.interface: a documented hand-off between engines that looks like an overlap and is not one: from reads to

interfaces.summary: Death to fate: Reality decides biological failure, with a crisis before every death; the pirate fate system decides what a dead character becomes. The two rules are compatible (Rex, 2026-10-30). This is a hand-off, never an overlap: the plugin reads the death, and Reality never reads the fate.

Character sheet as a view (Rex, 2026-10-30): a character sheet is a view of the three organism records, never a second source of numbers. STATS.md attributes (Rex's gameplay design: scale, Poise, Efficiency) are computed from the records through the pirate adapter; nobody inherits a Strength score.

Contact to injury: Physical Reality emits a contact event (position, relative velocity, direction, duration, impulse, penetration); anatomy and medicine read it to make the wound; materials read it for damage to objects and armour. Physical Reality never decides the wound; medicine never recomputes the impact.

Contact to the combat plugin: the pirate combat rules read the contact event for hit location and impact instead of rolling them (supersedes the plugin's regional dip as the source of hit location); combat keeps its own rules for turns, actions and choices.
